questions: Is a hangover just being thirsty, and does drinking water fix it?
short: Not just thirst, it seems. Thirst was clearly up only in the morning, but the hangover lasted all day. No experiment had tested water by mid-2024.
but: It all comes from one review, partly its authors' own second look at a walking study.

questions: If poppers hurt my eyes, does stopping them or lutein help?
short: Nobody knows yet, for either. Eye scans improved in 46 of 75 people checked again, but no report compared stopping poppers with carrying on.
but: These are case reports with no comparison group. Whether people really stopped was recorded for only 27 of 113.

questions: Do people's own habits lower the harms of benzos?
short: Nobody knows yet. A 2025 review of benzo harm reduction found no study that checked whether any habit lowers harm.
but: It's what people said and what researchers suggest, from one review. It didn't check how good its sources were.

questions: Does smoking cannabis cause lung cancer?
short: Nobody knows yet. Six studies put together found no clear link; a Swedish study found about twice the rate in men who'd used cannabis over 50 times.
but: Of those men, 91 in 100 also smoked tobacco, so the two can't be pulled apart.

questions: What was EVALI, the 2019 lung injury linked to THC vapes?
short: A 2019 US outbreak of serious lung injury in people who vaped; some died. Most said they'd vaped THC. The main suspect is an additive, vitamin E acetate.
but: None of these studies tested whether breathing it in causes the injury. And other chemicals aren't ruled out.

questions: Is vaping cannabis linked to breathing problems?
short: Yes, in one survey. About 1 in 4 who'd vaped cannabis in the past month reported a lasting cough, phlegm or bronchitis, against 1 in 8 who never had.
but: It's only what people said, once: nobody tested their lungs. So it can't show cause.

questions: What goes wrong with cannabis edibles, compared with smoking or vaping?
short: Different things. In one US ER, visits after edibles were more often for being too high, or for sudden mental-health or heart symptoms. After smoking or vaping: vomiting.
but: These are shares of ER visits, not risks. Nobody counted how many people used each form.

questions: Nicotine patch, gum or both: which works best for quitting smoking?
short: A nicotine patch plus nicotine gum or similar did a little better than one alone. About 17 in 100 quit for 6 months or more, against 14.
but: Most people in these trials smoked about 20 or more cigarettes a day. So they say little about lighter smoking.

questions: Do nicotine vapes work better than patches or gum for quitting smoking?
short: Yes, somewhat. In trials, about 4 more people in 100 quit for 6 months or more with a nicotine vape than with nicotine patches or gum.
but: In most trials that checked, more people kept using the vape than kept using patches or gum. And effects over years aren't known.

questions: Does vaping put fewer toxic chemicals in your body than smoking?
short: Mostly yes. But not clearly less nicotine. In a US survey, people who only vaped had about 98% less of one cancer-linked chemical than people who only smoked.
but: These are chemical levels, not illness. And in surveys, people who both vaped and smoked didn't have the lower levels.

questions: Are cannabis concentrates like wax and shatter riskier than flower?
short: Nobody knows yet. In one study, people using cannabis concentrates had over twice the blood THC of people using flower. Yet they didn't rate themselves higher.
but: It's one study of 121 people who use cannabis often, followed for just an hour.

questions: Does stronger cannabis make dependence more likely?
short: Some studies link them: in four of six, people who used stronger cannabis, like skunk, had more signs of a use disorder. None could show cause.
but: All six asked people once and took their word for how strong their cannabis was. Nobody measured THC.

questions: Does loperamide help with opioid withdrawal?
short: We can't say. The one study we read didn't check if loperamide eased opioid withdrawal.
but: It only counted people who saw a poisons doctor. And it had no group to compare them with.

questions: Do bedtime routines help children on ADHD stimulants fall asleep?
short: Maybe a little. With a set routine, children on ADHD stimulants fell asleep in 69 minutes on average, down from 92. Most still took at least an hour.
but: There was no comparison group, so part of the change may have happened anyway. For example, children were picked when their sleep was at its worst.

questions: How much does smoking cigarettes shorten life?
short: About 11 to 12 years on average, a big US study estimates. That's the gap between people who smoked cigarettes and people who never did.
but: These are group averages from one US study. They're not a forecast for any one person.

questions: Is it the nicotine or the smoke that does the harm?
short: In the US, burned tobacco causes most of tobacco's harm, a big report says. But it judges that nicotine alone can still harm an unborn baby.
but: It doesn't say how much of smoking's harm comes from nicotine itself.

questions: Is secondhand tobacco smoke really harmful?
short: Yes, two big US reports judge. Others' tobacco smoke is linked to sudden infant death, and to lung cancer and heart disease in adults who don't smoke.
but: These are the reports' judgments of other studies, so the figures are second-hand. And the later report builds on the earlier.

questions: Are cigars bad for you?
short: It seems so. In big US studies, people who smoked only cigars died of mouth cancer 4 to 8 times as often as people who never smoked.
but: The studies began decades ago, mostly with white men who smoked big cigars. And the review of them didn't compare cigars with cigarettes.

questions: Is snus bad for you?
short: It may be. Among Swedish men who never smoked, those who used snus died at a rate about 28% higher than men who used no tobacco.
but: This can't show snus caused it: men who used snus also drank more. And no source we read compared their death rate with people who smoke.

questions: Are nicotine pouches safe?
short: Nobody knows yet. No study has followed people who use nicotine pouches for more than 6 months, or looked at disease or death.
but: Most of what's known comes from lab tests and surveys, not from people's health. And the products differ a lot.

questions: What side effects do nicotine patches and gum have?
short: Irritation where they're used: the skin for nicotine patches, the mouth for nicotine gum. Chest pain or a pounding heart: 2.5 in 100, against 1.4 without.
but: These come from trials lasting weeks to months. Serious problems were too rare to compare.

questions: Do nicotine vapes actually help people quit smoking?
short: It may help. In trials, about 4 more in 100 quit for 6 months or more when given a nicotine vape than with counselling alone or nothing.
but: People knew they got a vape, and the vape groups got more support too. So part of the gap may come from the extra help.

questions: Is it safe to use a nicotine vape to quit smoking?
short: Nobody knows for sure. In quit-smoking trials, serious health problems were about as common with nicotine vapes as with patches or gum: 7 against 6 in 100.
but: Serious problems were few, and the trials lasted 2 years at most. That's too few and too short to show rare or later harms.

questions: Do nicotine pouches help people stop smoking?
short: Nobody knows yet. Four small trials couldn't tell whether nicotine pouches help people stop smoking or cut down. Ten more were under way in early 2025.
but: Three of the four trials took people who weren't planning to quit, and none lasted over 8 weeks.

questions: Does vaping cause heart or lung disease?
short: Nobody knows yet. A big US study found no clear rise in heart disease with vaping alone, and more lung problems that past smoking may explain.
but: It's one study of illnesses people reported, over 4 years at most. Just 41 people who only vaped got heart disease or a stroke: too few to tell.

questions: Is vaping as addictive as smoking?
short: Less, it seems, but still common. 77 in 100 people who only vaped daily said they felt dependent, against 94 in 100 who only smoked daily.
but: Nearly all who vaped had smoked before. And this US survey is from 2013 to 2014, before disposables and newer liquids were common.

questions: Does vaping harm people nearby?
short: Nobody knows yet. No study we read checked their health. Vaping does add nicotine and tiny particles to the air, but less than cigarette smoke.
but: The studies were small and lasted minutes to hours. None followed people nearby for weeks or years.

questions: How much less harmful is vaping than smoking?
short: Nobody knows yet. Vaping exposes people to far less of many smoke chemicals than smoking. But the famous 95% less harmful figure is disputed.
but: No study we read counted illness or death in people who vape over many years.

questions: Does a short burst of exercise help with the urge to smoke?
short: Right afterwards, it seems to. In trials, people rated their urge to smoke lower after short exercise, mostly walking or cycling, than after sitting still.
but: The urge was rated only once, minutes later, and people knew they had exercised. No study here checked whether it helps people quit.

questions: Does nicotine gum or an inhaler ease the first week of quitting?
short: For some symptoms, it seems so. All 9 trials that reported on grumpiness found less of it with nicotine gum, inhalers or tablets than with a dummy.
but: The review only counted which trials found a difference, not how big it was. And a drug company paid for it.

questions: Do ordinary laxatives from the shop help constipation caused by opioids?
short: We can't say yet. The one review we read on opioid constipation had no trials of laxatives from the shop.
but: What we read has no data on it, only its authors' remarks. One of them rests on two reviews we haven't read.

questions: What helps people get through a difficult psychedelic trip?
short: Looking back, people most often say letting go or calming the mind helped them through a hard psychedelic trip. None of it was tested.
but: These are memories, sometimes years old, from people who chose to answer. Saying something helped may just reflect how the trip ended.

questions: Do harm reduction habits mean fewer difficult psychedelic trips?
short: Nobody can say yet. In one survey, a higher score for safety habits went with a slightly easier first psychedelic trip. Not clearly the latest, though.
but: People recalled habits and trips at one sitting, often years later. And people who quit after a hard first trip couldn't take part.

questions: Do habits meant to make drinking less harmful help?
short: Not clearly. Teaching students bundles of habits, like pacing or eating, barely changed their drinking, by their own account. No trial tested one habit alone.
but: Nearly all were US college students. And every result is what they said about themselves.

questions: What do people do before and after ecstasy to lower harm?
short: Most said they drank water, took less ecstasy or took breaks, in one 2004 Australian survey. It didn't test whether any of it helps.
but: The 116 people chose to answer, and some came through an ecstasy website. So they may care more about harm reduction than others.

questions: Does vaped cannabis feel different from smoked?
short: It can. In one small lab study, the same cannabis felt stronger vaped than smoked, and raised heart rate more, but only at the lower of two amounts.
but: It's one study of 17 people who rarely use cannabis. Its authors say earlier studies found the two much alike.

questions: Do cannabis edible labels show how much THC is inside?
short: Mostly not, in a 2014 US test. Only 17 in 100 cannabis edibles matched their THC label; 60 in 100 held less and 23 in 100 more.
but: It's one test of 75 edibles, not picked at random, from markets its authors call unregulated. Products and rules may have changed since.
